title: How early should you arrive at Norwich Airport?
author: Brogan
cover_image_alt: Silhouettes of passengers waiting by the tall windows of a quiet departure lounge, reflected in a shiny floor
intro: Norwich Airport asks passengers to check in at least 2 hours before their flight, and as a small, one-terminal airport, that's usually plenty. Here's how the timings work, the liquids rule and how to get there.
seo_description: Norwich Airport advises checking in at least 2 hours before your flight. Liquids are still 100ml in a clear bag. Timings, security and getting there.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Airport advice:** at least 2 hours
- **Hand luggage, domestic:** often less in practice
- **Early morning waves:** add 30 mins
- **Liquids:** 100ml, in a clear bag

The 2-hour figure is Norwich Airport's own advice for checking in. The deadlines that matter most are your airline's check-in and bag drop times, which are in your booking. Rules can change, so check with the airport or your airline before you fly. We checked the details below in November 2026.

sections.heading: Why Norwich is usually quick
sections.text:
Norwich is a small regional airport with one terminal, a few miles north of the city centre. The walk from check-in to security to the gates is short, and on most days queues are too.

The busy times are the early morning departures, when the first flights of the day leave close together, and summer Saturdays, when holiday flights are busiest. Even then, the airport's 2-hour advice usually leaves time for a coffee.

sections.heading: How early for your flight
sections.text:
| Flight | Example | Our suggestion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Amsterdam with KLM | Onward connections worldwide | 2 hours, more if checking bags through |
| Domestic and Channel Islands | Loganair, including Jersey | 1½ to 2 hours |
| Summer holiday flights | Package and sun routes | 2 hours, 2½ on busy Saturdays |

The KLM flights to Amsterdam are Norwich's link to the world: you can check in for a long-haul trip on one ticket and change at Schiphol. If you do, allow the full 2 hours, as your bags and passport will be checked for your final destination.

Tip: if you're connecting at Amsterdam, check the minimum connection time on your booking. Schiphol is big, and moving between piers can take longer than you'd expect.

sections.heading: Security and liquids
sections.text:
When we checked, Norwich hadn't yet changed its security rules for the new generation of scanners. Its own guidance said the standard rules still apply until its new equipment is in place:

- **Liquids:** containers of 100ml or less, in a single clear resealable bag of about 1 litre.
- **Electronics:** take laptops and other large electrical items out of your bag for screening.
- **Larger liquids:** pack them in your hold bag.

Watch out: some UK airports now allow bigger liquids or let you leave them in your bag, so the rules at your destination may differ from Norwich. Pack for the strictest rule and you won't have to throw anything away.

sections.heading: Getting to Norwich Airport
sections.text:
The airport is on the northern edge of the city, about four miles from the centre, just off the outer ring road.

- **By car:** the airport has its own car parks next to the terminal, and booking ahead online is usually cheaper. Check the airport's website for drop-off arrangements and charges.
- **By bus or Park and Ride:** local buses and the airport Park and Ride site serve the area, but timetables change, so check the current service before relying on it for an early flight.
- **By taxi:** about 15 to 20 minutes from Norwich railway station, depending on traffic.

For a first-wave flight, most people drive or take a taxi, as buses may not run early enough.

sections.heading: Disruption and cancellations
sections.text: Small airports have fewer flights, so a cancellation can mean a long wait for the next one. Norwich posts notices about cancelled flights and disruption on its passenger information page, and KLM's Amsterdam flights have occasionally been cancelled because of bad weather at Schiphol. Before you leave home, check your flight status with your airline, and keep your booking reference and travel insurance details handy in case you need to rebook.

sections.heading: Where could you go from Norwich?
sections.text:
Norwich's routes are small but useful:

- **A weekend away:** [Amsterdam](/destinations/amsterdam), or connect onwards with KLM
- **A short island break:** Jersey, with Loganair
- **Summer sun:** check the airport's current list for holiday routes such as [Mallorca](/destinations/mallorca) or [Tenerife](/destinations/tenerife)

For more choice, [Stansted](/blog/where-can-you-fly-direct-from-stansted-airport) is about 1½ hours away by car. If you can't agree where to go, read our guide to [deciding where to go on holiday](/how-to-decide-where-to-go-on-holiday), or put your shortlist into a draw on somewhere.party.

faqs.question: How early should I get to Norwich Airport?
faqs.answer: Norwich Airport advises checking in at least 2 hours before your flight. Add 30 minutes for early morning flights and busy summer Saturdays.

faqs.question: What is the liquids limit at Norwich Airport?
faqs.answer: When we checked, Norwich still used the standard rule: containers of 100ml or less in a clear 1-litre bag, with laptops out for screening. Check the airport's website before you fly.

faqs.question: Where can you fly from Norwich Airport?
faqs.answer: KLM flies to Amsterdam, with onward connections worldwide, and Loganair flies to UK and Channel Islands destinations including Jersey. Holiday routes vary by season.

faqs.question: Is Norwich Airport busy?
faqs.answer: Usually not. It's a small, one-terminal airport, and queues are short outside the early morning and summer Saturday peaks.
